Subject: FinTrust - Data access controls & support access (post-call follow-up)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call focused on data handling and access controls so we're all aligned and can get you the artifacts you requested:

Key items you mentioned on the call:
- PII handling: determine what data Redwood will see and retention window for logs/PII-derived artifacts
- Data residency: US-only production region
- RBAC: role matrix for API, console, and support access; least-privilege enforcement
- Support access / break-glass: need an auditable, time-limited path for support with approvals and notification
- Audit logs & retention: visibility into admin actions and access events

Next steps from our side (aiming to deliver by EOD Monday unless you prefer otherwise):
1) RBAC matrix (roles -> permissions) + short diagram (RBAC-matrix.pdf)
2) SOC2 summary and relevant controls (SOC2-summary.pdf)
3) Draft break-glass runbook that outlines request/approval/audit flow (break-glass-runbook-draft.docx)
4) Schedule a 30-45 minute follow-up compliance call to walk the documents and demo audit logs - please share preferred windows next week.

If I missed anything from today’s conversation, please flag it. We’ll also loop in our security engineer (Dev) on the technical details.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: FinTrust - Data access controls & support access (post-call follow-up)

Thanks Marissa — that captures it well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PII: we need assurance that any PII extracted by the model or included in request/response logs can be redacted or retained per policy. For logs, FinTrust requires 90-day retention for request/response audit logs, and 365 days for admin change logs.
- Data residency: production data must remain within US regions; backups in ECS are allowed only if encrypted with customer-managed keys.
- RBAC details: we expect a role matrix that clearly separates "support read-only", "support elevated (time-limited)", and "admin" - with examples of API scopes for each.
- Break-glass: the flow should require a two-person approval (requester + security approver) and generate an immutable audit trail with the reason for access and duration.

Also please share any SOC2 Type II evidence or the mapping to the specific controls related to access control and logging. If you can include example log entries (redacted) in the audit logs demo, that would be helpful.

Available windows for a follow-up: Mon Nov 23 after 10am PT, Tue Nov 24 morning, or Wed Nov 25 1-3pm PT.

Alex
Head of Security Operations
FinTrust
alex.johnson@fintrust.com

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 5:03 PM Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintrust.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — that captures it well. A few clarifications from our side: ...

Thanks Alex — good notes. A few quick technical responses and confirmations from the Redwood infra/security side:

- PII & logs: our platform supports redaction and field masking at ingestion and at the tokenization layer for specific fields. We can provide examples of both masked log entries and raw entries (redacted) in the audit demo.
- Retention: audit logs and admin change logs are configurable per-customer; default retention is 90 days for request logs and 365 for admin events - we can set per your policy and export archived logs on request.
- Data residency & keys: we support customer-managed KMS (Bring Your Own Key) and will restrict primary storage to US regions for this tenancy.
- RBAC & break-glass: proposed implementation: ephemeral elevated role (time-limited AWS STS-style token) with a dual-approval webhook (request -> security approver + product owner). All actions performed under break-glass are tagged, recorded in an immutable audit stream, and flagged for post-incident review.

I’ll prepare the RBAC matrix and a short diagram of the break-glass flow. Two clarifying asks for FinTrust before we finalize the runbook: 
1) Who are the required approvers (email addresses/titles) for the two-person approval?
2) Any max-duration requirement for break-glass sessions (e.g., 15/30/60 minutes)?

Happy to jump on the compliance call during the windows Alex suggested.

-Dev
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
